sources.entry: Crafty Controller - Minecraft launcher and manager that allows users to start and administer Minecraft servers from a user-friendly interface. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/Python

summary.name: Crafty Controller
summary.one_liner: Crafty Controller is a free, open-source, web-based Minecraft server launcher and manager for starting and administering Minecraft servers from a self-hosted panel.
use_cases: Running multiple Minecraft servers on different versions
Managing players and running server commands from a browser
Editing server settings and files through a web file manager
Hosting a Minecraft server on a home network with port forwarding
summary.what_it_does: Crafty Controller runs as a self-hosted web server, accessible on the local network by default and optionally port-forwarded for external access. From its web interface you can create and run servers, manage players, run commands, change server settings, view and edit server files, and make backups. It runs any Minecraft server that uses a jar file, and can also run Bedrock executables. Installation is supported through Linux deployment scripts, Windows executables, and Docker.
notable: Licensed under GPL-3.0 with full source code available on GitLab
Self-hosted with data stored locally; uses Argon2 password hashing and SSL-secured webserver by default
Built-in file manager and a mobile app for monitoring servers
Free support from volunteers in the Crafty Discord
caveats: Some server types (e.g. Paper, Spigot, Waterfall, ATM3) are harder to set up, and the page says it requires a bit of technical knowledge
External access outside the local network requires port forwarding
Page describes Crafty 4 as a beta overview
